_doc: Củng Tinh Quán lineage (rules-proposals R5). Leans Earth, Metal (unchanged; the seat passes, Earth 45 %, Metal 21 %). Outer gate: star-pacing-primer (proposal, Yellow, Earth or Metal). Inner gate and above: bowing-stars-canon (proposal, Earth tier, Earth). Secret arts: armillary-array-canon (proposal, inner gate; the abbey's formation craft), star-lake-mirror (proposal, the head's divination; it reads by Earth and Metal, and Light, if the holder has it, reads further). The head's old aux deep-vein-scripture is the Pivot's head-only secret and is replaced (see his 'changed' note). Unpriced.

secret.note: the abbey's formation craft, taught to every inner Daoist
the head's divination; it reads the lake by Earth and the star-iron rim, and a holder with Light reads further

lineage.tree_route_note: The abbey's road: Heavy as a Mountain for the slow weight of the Stars Bow, Array Foundation for the armillary rings, Gazing Peak for the star-reader's thần thức and formation power.

techniques.name: Star-Pacing Primer (Bộ Cương Quyết)
techniques.concept: The outer gate's method is a walk: the novice paces the seven stars of the Dipper on a pattern cut into the abbey's courtyard, one step to a breath, drawing Earth up through the feet or Metal down from the night air. The Daoists call it walking the handle (bộ cương đạp đẩu). In a fight the holder's footwork lays a small pattern on the ground; standing on it steadies them.

arts.concept: Each of your next seven arts leaves a mark; on the seventh the marks join into a Field: on rising it gives the foe one Slowed Time stack, and you take less damage while it holds.

techniques.lore: As old as the abbey. Every Daoist of Củng Tinh has walked the courtyard pattern at dusk every day of their lives; the stones are worn a hand deep where the seventh star is.

techniques.name: Bowing Stars Canon (Củng Tinh Kinh)
techniques.concept: Named from the Analects: the pole star keeps its place and the stars bow to it. The cultivator makes their dantian a fixed point and lets the qi around them turn on it, slowly, like the sky on the pole. In a fight the holder does not move much; Earth weight gathers around them, foes who circle them are dragged inward and slowed, and the longer the holder stands, the heavier their strikes become.

arts.concept: A slow field around the holder: foes inside are pulled toward them and slowed, and gain Earth stacks each second they stay.
After 3 s Still, your Earth arts deal more damage and you are Planted, with more timer resistance; it resets when you stop being Still.

techniques.lore: Written by the founder Lệnh Hồ Chiêm in the abbey's first century, after thirty years of watching the Dipper turn in the lake of Tinh Lạc Hồ (A205). It is the same idea as the Pivot's own, older and slower.

techniques.name: Armillary Array Canon (Tuyền Cơ Trận Kinh)
techniques.concept: The abbey's formation craft. Arrays are laid as rings, like the rings of the armillary, each ring a star-hour. In a fight an array laid by it turns as the fight runs, one star-hour to every 5 s, and each ring is strongest in the hour it was laid. In a fight the holder throws rings of star-iron discs that lock together around a foe.

arts.concept: Lays a ring array around a foe: while inside they deal less damage and take Earth damage at each tick; a second ring laid on the first doubles both.
Rotates every array the holder has laid, moving them a step and refreshing their duration.

A passive art. Each ring belongs to the 5 s hour of the fight in which it was laid and is strongest in that hour. When rings of three different hours stand at once, the armillary turns: every ring is refreshed, and each further hour adds damage and slows the foe.

techniques.lore: Taught with the star iron of Vẫn Tinh Khoáng (A206): the abbey's array discs are cut from it, and they ring faintly when an array turns.

techniques.name: Mirror of the Star-Fallen Lake (Tinh Lạc Kính Quyết)
techniques.concept: The head's divination. The holder reads the Dipper in the water of Tinh Lạc Hồ through a star-iron rim, by Earth and Metal rather than by eye, and reads in it what the armillary only points at. A holder with Light reads further in it. In a fight it shows the holder the foe's next art a moment before it comes.

arts.concept: For a few seconds the holder sees each foe's next art before it is cast: they evade or ward it far more easily, and their counter-strikes against it are critical.
Names one foe: that foe's buffs are dimmed and their luck in the fight (khí vận) is lowered for a long while.

techniques.lore: Taught by the founder to Thẩm Bắc Thần. It needs only the abbey's Earth and the Metal of Vẫn Tinh's iron; Thẩm's thread of Light lets him read further in it than any head before him. It is how he saw the omen of 1188 that he has told no one.
